title: Serial overhead around seeding and setup
body:
On a 481.8 s search of all Pfam against one MGnify recall shard of 2,455,940 targets at 48 threads, the `-s` runtime tree shows 30 s of serial work, 6.2% of the run. Two items make up 72% of it, and both have known fixes:

| item | seconds | issue |
|---|---|---|
| mmseqs target db write | 15.5 | nail-fc2ac4 |
| profile parse in `build_pipeline` | 6.2 | nail-65ce8f |

The rest of the serial work sums to 1.7% of the run. The tree and the breakdown are in the notes. nail-7ea5c0 decided that moving nail's io onto `libsail` is separate work, now nail-167dd7, and neither fix waits on it.

## Out of scope

- Caching the target db across runs. It helps only repeated runs, and those do not matter here.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text:
Serial time on the 481.8 s run:

| item | seconds | share of run |
|---|---|---|
| db write | 15.5 | 3.2% |
| pipeline build | 6.2 | 1.3% |
| slice, decide and merge | 3.4 | 0.7% |
| query and target index | 2.7 | 0.6% |
| seed index | 1.6 | 0.3% |
| convertalis | 0.7 | 0.1% |
| all serial | 30.1 | 6.2% |

Removing every item entirely would buy 6%. Below the two large items, the 2026-09-28 code survey found these mechanisms:

- `PrefilterDb` in `mmseqs.rs` reopens its file on every `get` and `next_n`. Its `from_path` validates every record with an open, a seek and a one-byte read. It scans for newlines by hand, and all of it runs on one thread between align calls. A held handle or a map, `memchr`, and rayon over queries would speed up slice, decide and merge together, worth about 3 s.
- The slice writes a record for `Terminated` queries too, per the TODO in `seed_stage.rs`.
- `Seeds::from_path` allocates a `String` and a `Vec` per TSV line, on one thread.
- The index passes run on one thread, because `from_path` hard-codes `CHUNKS=1`. The HMM index does a `strum` match per line, and nail then reads the HMM file a second time to parse profiles. One pass that indexes and parses would remove the second read.
- nail could read the per-iteration align dbs into `Seeds` directly and drop `convertalis` and the merge. That gains about 1 s and costs a parser for mmseqs's alignment record. These numbers do not justify it.

For proportion, the prefilter takes 225 s, 47% of the run, all inside mmseqs. The alignment stage at 93% busy idles about 12 s.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text:
Rerun at `92de7c5`, after the libsail io commits, on the 16-core box at `-t 8`. The box has 8 physical cores. Inputs are the same 20,795 Pfam profiles against the same 2,455,940 targets, with native mmseqs `8cc5ce3`. The run took 726.1 s and reported 3,031,620 hits. The log and the full tree are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-serial-overhead` on that box.

The two runs used different machines and thread counts, so the old column is a rough guide. It is not a before and after.

| item | 48 threads at `432ff65`, s | 8 threads at `92de7c5`, s |
|---|---|---|
| db write | 15.47 | 7.31 |
| target index | 1.16 | 3.36 |
| pipeline build | 6.23 | 3.07 |
| slice, decide and merge | 3.40 | 1.25 |
| seed index | 1.64 | 0.56 |
| convertalis | 0.65 | 0.38 |
| query index | 1.53 | 0.09 |
| all serial | 30.08 | 16.02 |

The serial work is 2.2% of this run. At 48 threads the parallel stages shrink, and the same 16 s would come to roughly 3 to 4% of the run. That figure is an estimate from scaling and was not measured.

- db write is still the largest item, nail-fc2ac4.
- target index went up from 1.16 s to 3.36 s, while query index fell from 1.53 s to 0.09 s. A warm rerun with a one-profile query gave 3.24 and 3.35 s, so the page cache does not explain it. About 2.2 s of it is the duplicate-name check in `Records::map`, nail-cfade0.
- pipeline build is 3.07 s, nail-65ce8f.
- The alignment stage reported 99.6% busy at 8 threads. The idle time in nail-ec7764 does not show up at this thread count.

Progressive seeding ran 11 align iterations for 67.1 s, all inside `mmseqs align`, which runs on 8 threads. The prefilter took 187.6 s.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text: Serial items after commits `a8a28e5` through `f337e0f` on `dev`, on the 16-core box at `-t 8` with 2,455,940 targets. The query profile db is not timed on its own. Target index 3.36 s became 0.37 s, from the sharded repeated-name check in nail-cfade0 and libsail 0.4.2. Pipeline build 3.07 s became under 0.01 s, since nail-65ce8f and nail-811f24 parse the hmm queries once, in parallel. Query index grew from 0.09 s to 0.50 s because it now includes that parse. The db write leaf went from 7.31 s to about 1.2 s: the target db write fell from about 4.3 s to 1.05 s in nail-fc2ac4, and the profile db stopped parsing. The largest serial items left are slice, decide and merge at 1.25 s, seed index at 0.60 s and convertalis at 0.38 s. The db write leaf is an estimate from the one-profile run plus the profile db; no full run has measured it since `f337e0f`.
